extracted.intended_audience: Members of the European Parliament (JURI), legal/policy advisers, national patent offices, patent practitioners and other stakeholders interested in the European patent system
extracted.subtask_description: In-depth policy analysis of the European Patent Organisation, the European Patent Office (EPO), the existing European (bundle) patent system and the new Unitary Patent/Unified Patent Court package (regulations, translation rules, fees, governance and transitional arrangements). Intended to inform legislative and oversight decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to obtain a European patent (filing routes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPpatent can be obtained in one of two ways: (a) European route: direct European patent application (EPC application granted for some or all contracting states to the EPC); (b) International route: European patent application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking worldwide protection may use the services of the EPO which files, searches and examines under the PCT. Annex/Figure distinguishes direct European filings vs PCT international filings (2014 figures: ~60,000 direct EPC filings and ~214,000 PCT filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and internal legal remedies to safeguard patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may oppose a EPpatent within a period of 9 months from the mention of its grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO publishes opposition statistics (opposition rates and number of decisions). Opposed patents may be upheld as granted or in amended form (around 70% upheld in 2013). Decisions in examination and opposition may be appealed to the Boards of Appeal; Boards settled ~2,100 cases in 2013. Note: Boards of Appeal are independent but integrated into the EPO organisational structure; appeals to external bodies (e.g., ILO) are possible but may be lengthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: European patent is a bundle requiring national validation
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'European Patent' granted by the EPO constitutes a bundle of national patents because it must be validated by each state in which the applicant wishes protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After grant the proprietor must choose which Contracting States to validate in; litigation on bundle patents is (currently) heard before relevant national courts, i.e., separate proceedings in each national jurisdiction unless and until alternative regimes (e.g., UPC/unitary patent) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary Patent (European patent with unitary effect) — post-grant registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012 an application for a 'European patent with unitary effect' is filed at the EPO as with current procedure; once granted and registered in the European Patent Register it takes effect in the participating Member States of the EU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To gain UPP the EPpatent must have been granted with the same set of claims for all participating Member States. The unitary patent provides uniform protection and equal effect in participating Member States and does not require validation in each individual member state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation arrangements for unitary patent (claims and languages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation (EU) No 1260/2012 allows patent applications in any language, with a translation into one of the EPO's official languages (EN, FR, DE). The applicant has to translate the patent claims into the two remaining EPO languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation costs would be covered for certain EU residents filing in another EU language. No further translation is needed unless required in specific litigation. The European Parliament secured full reimbursement of translation costs for EU-based SMEs, non-profit organisations, universities and public research organisations and a compensation scheme with a ceiling for certain filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional translation arrangements for unitary patent (temporary additional translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: As from application of the UPP regulations there will be a transitional period of six to a maximum of twelve years during which the patent holder will need to file a translation of the patent specification into one additional language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is granted in German or French the translation shall be into English; if granted in English, the translation shall be into any other official language of the EU at the patent holder's choice. These translations are for information purposes only and do not have legal effect. After the transitional period no translations will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Patent Court (UPC) — jurisdiction and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement on the Unified Patent Court (UPCtA) creates a specialised patent court (UPC) with exclusive jurisdiction for litigation relating to European patents and European patents with unitary effect (unitary patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UPC will comprise Court of First Instance (CFI) with a central division (Paris seat, specialist sections in London and Munich) and local/regional divisions, plus a Court of Appeal (Luxembourg). UPC will hear validity and infringement of unitary and European bundle patents and also actions concerning infringement and validity of Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs) based on European bundle patents and unitary patents. UPC will not have competence over national patent rights granted by national patent offices. Any ruling by the UPC on a patent will be simultaneously valid in all countries in which that patent has been validated and enforcement follows national law where enforcement takes place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of central division cases by technology (IPC-based allocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases will be allocated to each section of the central division according to technology sectors as defined by the International Patent Classification (IPC) applied to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: London will hear cases relating to chemistry, including pharmaceuticals and life sciences (patents classified under IPC classes A and C); Munich will hear cases relating to mechanical engineering (IPC class F); all other cases will be heard by the Paris central division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional period and opt-out from UPC jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: During a transitional period of at least seven years (extendable by a further seven), infringement and validity actions on European bundle patents may still be brought before national courts. An owner of an EPpatent may opt out of the jurisdiction of the UPC on a patent-by-patent basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once opted out the European bundle patent remains under national courts. A patent can be opted back in at any time before the end of the transitional period, provided no action has already been brought before a national court (Art. 58 para. 4 UPCtA). These transitional arrangements do not apply to the new unitary patent (cases for unitary patents will always be heard by the UPC). The opt-out provision is motivated by industry concerns about central invalidation by a new court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting criteria for the unitary patent (Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for setting the fees for the UPP can be found at Article 12 of the unitary patent regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee-setting process must take into account administration costs, the size of the market and the level of fees paid for current European bundle patents. The specific amounts/structure were to be decided (document notes decision expected end of 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Levying of fees under the EPC (renewal fee proportion to Organisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 39 EPC, each Contracting State pays to the Organisation, for each European patent maintained in that state, a proportion of its national renewal fee fixed by the Administrative Council and which may not exceed 75% and is the same for all Contracting States (proportion has been 50% since 1984).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If that proportion is less than a uniform minimum fixed by the Administrative Council, the Contracting State must pay that minimum. The national patent offices make payments to the EPOrg on a quarterly basis. The structure and level of national renewal fees are fixed by the Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO budget and self-financing principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO is self-financing, covering all operating and capital expenditure from the fees paid by users for its services; the 2015 budget cited was EUR 2 billion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 37(c) EPC provides that the Organisation's budget is financed, where necessary, by Contracting States. If the Organisation cannot balance its budget, Contracting States must remit special financial contributions (Article 40). Revenue composition (2013 figures): procedural fees ~EUR 1.5bn (incl. ~EUR 0.4bn national renewal fees and ~EUR 1.1bn procedural fees); other revenues include search services and information products. Major expense is staff costs (~EUR 1.37bn in 2013). As an intergovernmental organisation, the EPO cannot become insolvent because Contracting States are obliged to finance deficits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for identical claims to obtain unitary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to gain UPP the EPpatent must have been granted with the same set of claims for all the participating Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a formal requirement before a request for unitary effect will be accepted; it connects pre-grant examination under the EPC to post-grant unitary registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competences and governance powers of the Administrative Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council of the EPOrg exercises legislative powers for the Organisation and supervises the EPO; detailed provisions relate to Articles 26–36 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrative Council may amend time limits in the EPC, the Implementing Regulations, the EPO Financial Regulation, Service Regulations for employees, conditions of employment, salary scales and Rules relating to Fees. It may authorise the President to negotiate and, subject to approval, conclude agreements on behalf of EPOrg States. The document also records criticism about composition (many representatives are national patent office directors) and potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boards of Appeal independence and staff recourse limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on appeals are taken by the Boards of Appeal; Boards are independent but integrated into the organisational structure of the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO staff historically had limited practical external recourse because of the EPO's international status and immunity (appeals to the ILO Administrative Tribunal are possible but considered cumbersome and lengthy). The document recounts litigation around strike regulations and calls for improved social dialogue and formal recognition of trade unions to restore social peace.
